> **What this case shows** — the [Friedman sibling](../sway-4cond-friedman-bds/index.qmd) found the four
> vision × surface conditions differ in sway and gave a monotone rank order; *which* pairs differ, and does
> vision matter more on foam? Here the **Nemenyi** test — the repeated-measures post-hoc — answers it. The
> **newly-authored** `nemenyiTest` runs all 6 pairwise comparisons, reproducing **`PMCMRplus`**
> **bit-for-bit** and **`scikit_posthocs`** to machine precision. All six pairs differ, but the vision
> effect **depends on the surface**: eyes-open vs eyes-closed is only **borderline on firm ground**
> (p=0.044) yet **strong on foam** (p=3.1e-8) — when proprioception is degraded, balance leans much more on
> vision.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — the subjects × conditions matrix → `nemenyiTest()` → read the pairwise comparisons.
**Way of thinking** — Nemenyi is to Friedman what Tukey is to ANOVA and Dunn is to Kruskal-Wallis: the
family-wise-controlled post-hoc for its omnibus. Comparing the *same* effect (eyes-open vs eyes-closed)
across two surfaces reads off the sensory reweighting directly.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics()`, `PhysioAnalysis::nemenyiTest()`.
:::

## Proposition

In the Nemenyi post-hoc of COP path length across the four BDS conditions (n=158), all six condition pairs
differ, and the vision effect is much weaker on firm ground (Open-Firm vs Closed-Firm, p=0.044) than on foam
(Open-Foam vs Closed-Foam, p=3.1e-8); `nemenyiTest` reproduces `PMCMRplus::frdAllPairsNemenyiTest`
bit-for-bit and `scikit_posthocs.posthoc_nemenyi_friedman` to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is which conditions differ and how vision reweights with the surface.** The Friedman sibling
certified the omnibus difference and the rank order and deferred the pairwise structure; this fold performs
the post-hoc, authoring the Nemenyi op and resolving the open question.

## Challenge & approach

We take the same certified per-subject sway for the four conditions and run `nemenyiTest` — all 6 pairwise
comparisons from the within-block mean ranks, family-wise controlled — checking every p against
`PMCMRplus` and `scikit_posthocs`, and reading the eyes-open/closed contrast on firm vs foam.

```
158 subjects × 4 conditions (swayMetrics, certified) → nemenyiTest (6 comparisons)
  all 6 pairs significant; the vision effect by surface:
    firm ground:  Open-Firm vs Closed-Firm   p = 0.044   (borderline)
    foam:         Open-Foam vs Closed-Foam    p = 3.1e-8  (strong)
     vs PMCMRplus::frdAllPairsNemenyiTest        → max |p| = 0 (bit-for-bit)
     vs scikit_posthocs.posthoc_nemenyi_friedman → max |p| ~ 5e-13 (machine precision)
```

## Data

**Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS balance dataset (figshare)**: per subject, COP path length in each of the four
vision × surface quiet-standing conditions, for the 158 subjects with all four. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the Nemenyi −log10(adjusted p) matrix over the four conditions; a star marks significant pairs — all six differ. Right: the eyes-open/closed vision effect by surface — barely over the significance line on firm ground (p=0.044) but far above it on foam (p=3.1e-8), a ~6-order-of-magnitude difference.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* on the left, every off-diagonal cell is starred — the four conditions are pairwise
distinct. On the right, the same manipulation (closing the eyes) barely registers on firm ground yet
dominates on foam: with the feet's proprioception degraded, the balance system reweights toward vision.

| Comparison | p (adjusted) |
|---|--:|
| eyes-open vs eyes-closed, **firm** | **0.044** (borderline) |
| eyes-open vs eyes-closed, **foam** | **3.1e-8** (strong) |
| Open-Firm vs Closed-Foam (extreme) | ~0 (statistic 18.0) |
| pairs significant | **6 / 6** |
| vs `PMCMRplus` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-for-bit) |
| vs `scikit_posthocs` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~5e-13) |

Every comparison equals both references to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/nemenyi_summary.csv`](artifacts/nemenyi_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`nemenyiTest` completes the post-hoc set (Tukey for ANOVA, Dunn for Kruskal-Wallis, Nemenyi for Friedman) and
reproduces the reference on the certified `swayMetrics`. The transferable takeaway: **the same sensory
manipulation can matter enormously or barely at all depending on context. Here closing the eyes is nearly
inconsequential on firm ground but decisive on foam — a quantified read-out of how standing balance
reweights from proprioception to vision as the surface becomes unreliable.**

## Open questions

- The Nemenyi post-hoc quantifies the surface-dependent vision effect pairwise; a formal two-way (vision ×
  surface) model with an explicit interaction term would test the reweighting directly and give it an effect
  size. The distribution-free Nemenyi post-hoc is the honest first-line answer after Friedman. *Documented,
  not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Posturography sway metrics | `swayMetrics()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Friedman (omnibus, repeated measures) | `friedmanTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Nemenyi (post-hoc) | `nemenyiTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **adjusted p** — already family-wise controlled across all pairs; compare to your alpha directly.
- **same effect across contexts** — reading one manipulation (vision) across two surfaces is more
  informative than either alone; the gap is the reweighting.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

# M: subjects x conditions matrix of swayMetrics path lengths
nemenyiTest(M)   # a data frame of all pairwise statistics and family-wise-adjusted p -- bit-for-bit vs PMCMRplus
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/nemenyi_summary.csv`](artifacts/nemenyi_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
pairwise statistics and adjusted p-values, the bit-exact match against PMCMRplus and the machine-precision
match against scikit_posthocs, the firm-vs-foam vision-effect contrast, the significance count, and the
honestly noted scope (authors the new nemenyiTest op; sway from the certified swayMetrics; surface-dependent
vision reweighting; cross-sectional association).
